definitions.meaning: A force that moves something away from you: kicking a ball and shoving a box across a table are pushes.
A force that brings something closer to you: dragging a box towards you and reeling in a kite are pulls.
A force between two objects that are touching: every push, pull and rub of friction needs contact, unlike a magnet pulling iron across a small gap.
The rubbing force between surfaces that slide against each other: it pushes back against the sliding and slows things down.
The two ends of a magnet, marked N and S: opposite poles attract and like poles repel.
What opposite poles do: a north pole and a south pole facing each other pull together and snap onto each other.
What like poles do: two north poles, or two south poles, facing each other push each other apart.

mechanismSteps: Push and pull: a push moves the box away across the table and a pull drags it back closer - both are forces, and forces change how things move.
Friction slows things down: the block slides down the slope while the rough surface rubs against it, and the friction arrow pushes back against the slide.
Opposite poles attract: every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and when S faces N the magnets pull together and snap with a click.
Watch out: a magnet does not attract every metal: turn the magnet so N faces N and the magnets repel, and remember the magnet only pulls iron and a few metals, ignoring most things.
objectives: Tell a push from a pull and say what each does to an object
Explain how friction slows a sliding object down
State what happens when opposite poles and when like poles face each other
Name the metal a magnet reliably pulls and explain why not every metal is pulled
subject: science
title: Pushes, pulls, friction and magnets

trap.explanation: Magnets grab some metals so strongly that they feel like they grab all of them. Magnets ignore most things: they only pull iron and a few metals. In the animation scene s4 the warning is spelled out in the caption itself - a magnet does not attract every metal - so test each metal instead of trusting the shine.
trap.misconception: A magnet attracts every kind of metal.

workedExample: In scene s3, follow the magnets as a worked example: the south pole of one magnet faces the north pole of the other, so the opposite poles attract and the loose magnet slides across and snaps onto the first with a click. Each step is a check: read the pole labels, decide whether the facing poles are opposite or the same, then predict attract or repel before the magnets move.
